newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK TO AUCTION TWO-YEAR STATE BONDS MAY 6. [CORRECTED 14:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK TO AUCTION TWO-YEAR STATE BONDS MAY 6. [CORRECTED 14:45 GMT]

text.p: The Czech central bank on Tuesday said it will auction a five billion crown tranche of two year state bonds on May 6.
The central bank added in a statement that yield would be determined at the auction.
Bids for the paper will be accepted until 1100 GMT on May 5, it added.
In its last auction of similar bonds on November 5, maximum yield was set at 11.6 percent.
The bonds will be governed by Czech law and will be issued in book entry form.

Government bonds issued between August 1, 1993 and December 31, 1996 are not subject to the Czech 25 percent withholding tax. All government bonds after the end of 1996 are subject to a 25 percent withholding tax. (Corrects to clarify which bonds are subject to withholding tax.)
